title: Polynesian Navigators

cards.h: They crossed the biggest ocean on Earth with no maps, no compass, and no metal
cards.b:
Look at a map of the Pacific. A triangle with corners at Hawaii, New Zealand and Easter Island covers about 10 million square km, mostly sea. By around 1300 CE, Polynesians had settled all of it.

How? Stars, waves, birds and brilliance.

The ancestors came from island Southeast Asia. The Lapita people, known for stamped pottery, spread through Melanesia and then to Tonga and Samoa. After a pause, their descendants pushed east into the huge open ocean.

Navigators memorised the rising and setting points of stars. They read the shape of ocean swells, the flight of land birds at dawn and dusk, and clouds that stay above islands. A skilled navigator could sense land before seeing it.

They sailed double-hulled voyaging canoes with sails, carrying plants, pigs, chickens and families. This was planned settlement, not drifting.

Some Western scholars once thought the Polynesians could only have drifted by accident. In 1976 the canoe Hokule'a sailed from Hawaii to Tahiti without instruments, guided by the Micronesian navigator Mau Piailug. It proved intentional voyaging was possible.

Piailug, from Satawal, taught Hawaiian sailors their own lost art.

The sweet potato, from South America, was grown across Polynesia before Europeans came. In 2020 a genetic study (Ioannidis et al.) found Native American ancestry in some Polynesian islanders, from contact around 1200 CE.

So someone made contact. Who sailed which way is debated.

New Zealand, Aotearoa, was one of the last large places to be settled, around 1250-1300. The Maori developed their own culture there. Rapa Nui people carved the giant moai statues.

The tale that Rapa Nui 'collapsed itself' is debated. Researchers argue about the role of rats, European disease and slave raids.

In 1947 the Norwegian Thor Heyerdahl sailed the raft Kon-Tiki from Peru to prove South Americans settled Polynesia. A raft can drift, but language, DNA and archaeology show settlers came from the west.

Also, dates of settlement for Hawaii vary a lot by method and the numbers above are best estimates, not certain.

Five things to remember

  1. Lapita ancestors spread through the Pacific from about 1300 BCE.
  2. Navigators used stars, swells and birds.
  3. Hokule'a (1976) showed deliberate voyages were possible.
  4. DNA suggests contact with South America around 1200 CE.
  5. Austronesian sailors also reached Madagascar.

Think about it

  • How do you pass a skill down without writing?
  • Why is the 'accidental drift' idea so hard to believe now?
